I would have bowed very deeply before him, as he is -at least for me- one of the most important poets. But then I would have taken him by the hand: "There is nothing new under the sun," you wrote, Ecclesiastes. Nevertheless, You yourself were born new under the sun. And the poem you created is also new under the sun, as before You nobody had written it. [...] And also I would like to ask you, Ecclesiastes, what would you like to write now, again under the sun? Something with which to complete your ideas, or maybe you're tempted to deny some of them? [...] For you will not say "I have already written everything, I have nothing to add." No poet can say this, much less one as great as You. (I don't know, Wislawa Szymborska.) Of the following questions posed by the teacher, which one enables students to recognize the purpose of the dialogical sequence in the previous fragment?
choices: What register of speech does the broadcaster use to address Ecclesiastes?
What are the central themes addressed in Ecclesiastes' book according to the broadcaster?
What is the contrast that can be drawn between literary historians and Ecclesiastes?
What is the relationship between Ecclesiastes' reference and the idea of the transient nature of the poet's certainties?

question: Read the following situation: A high school teacher will assess the narrative genre unit with a final project that consists of analyzing a short story, distinguishing the following elements: – Type of literary world. – Temporal resources. – Type of setting. – Characterization of characters. – Type of narrator. Given the nature of the evaluation of this unit, what instrument should the teacher apply to assess and provide feedback on the work?
choices: Holistic rubric
Analytical rubric
Appreciation scale
Checklist

question: In reading a story, which of the following options corresponds to a reading strategy inherent in the holistic model?
choices: Underline the words in the story that represent the actions of the characters
Classify the characters in the story as main or secondary
Infer what the text is about based on its illustrations or other linguistic clues
Sequence the main events of the story according to their order in the narrative

question: A teacher from a 4th grade class has divided the class into groups to write a news article on different topics. Once they have written the body of the article, he observes the headlines each group is creating and notices that one of them wrote: “The zoo lion”. Seeing this, he decides to propose an activity to help them review and evaluate their headline. Which of the following activities is most suitable for this group of students to review and improve their headline according to the specific characteristics of this element of the news?
choices: Read with them the headlines of the news written by the other groups. Then, hand out the bodies of those articles and ask them to match each headline with the corresponding body
Read with them bodies of newspaper articles. Then, ask them to associate the headlines of these articles and discuss with their classmates how they knew these fragments matched the headlines

Read with them headlines of different news articles, such as: “Polar bear dies at the zoo”, “Albino rhino is born in Chile”. Then, ask them to distinguish the elements present in those headlines that are missing from theirs

Read with them the article they wrote. Then, ask them to take up the written headline and complete it by adding information, based on questions such as: “Where is the zoo located?”, “What is the lion like?”

question: A 4th grade basic education teacher is working with her students on understanding the grammatical agreement between the subject and the verb. For this purpose, she has decided to incorporate some activities during the reading of a short text that presents a single protagonist. Which of the following activities would be appropriate for the teacher to incorporate so that students work on the grammatical agreement between the subject and the verb?
choices: Underline the actions performed by the protagonist and rewrite them by changing the number of the subject
Select in the text the sentences where the protagonist appears and distinguish the subject from the predicate in each one
Highlight with different colors in the text the actions performed by the protagonist and conjugate them in a different tense
Enclose with a color the subjects of the sentences where the protagonist appears and replace them with the corresponding personal pronoun

question: A teacher of a 4th Grade class will start working on the function of the adverb with his students, so they can use them in their writings. As they have been working on reading comprehension from the story 'El Gatopato y la princesa Monilda' by María Elena Walsh, the teacher decides to select the following fragment of that text for his activity: For many days, Gatopato spent crying all the time in a shoe because he felt that nobody loved him. One day, Princess Monilda passed through the forest and saw him. She thought he was cute and wanted to have a Gatopato for a long time. So she gently picked him up, petted him, and took him to the palace. Which of the following tasks allows students to understand the function of the adverb from the fragment selected by the teacher?
choices: Explain why Gatopato was sad
Underline what Monilda thought when she saw Gatopato
Describe the way Monilda picked up Gatopato
Identify where Gatopato spent many days crying

question: In relation to the initiation to writing, which of the following educational situations is most suitable for promoting that children gradually produce their own graphic signs?
choices: That they copy short messages to record the results of their activities
That they draw and write in their sketchbook every day on topics of their interest
That they have laminated cards to freely practice arabesques and garlands
That they complete sequences of dots in worksheets, respecting the start and end points

question: A preschool teacher plans to work with her group on the following learning objective: "To discover, in playful contexts, phonological attributes of known words, such as identifying final sounds." Which of the following learning experiences is the most appropriate to work on the objective set by the teacher?
choices: Guess words that will be mentioned phoneme by phoneme
Discover words that form assonant rhymes within a poem
Physically represent the number of syllables in different words
Identify words that have the same sounds in different alliterations

question: A teacher in a 7th Grade class asks the students to write a news article about the school's anniversary week. The following is a fragment of a draft of the text written by one of the students. The Blue Alliance, after a close result, is the winner of the anniversary week. After a week of intense competitions, the Blue Alliance took first place in the 2017 anniversary. With a difference of only 100 points, the diligent Blue Alliance was crowned champion of the anniversary of the San Patricio school last week. Among the activities won by the Blue Alliance, the most outstanding was the dance of the kings, presenting a great choreography: the most coordinated, creative, and motivating of all. The 4th-year high school students, with great enthusiasm and joy, led the celebration of the victory and invited the other members of the Alliance to dance and sing with them. Considering the characteristics of the news article, what is the difficulty presented by the text written by the student?
choices: The description of the facts provides irrelevant data
The headline does not convey the central idea of the news
The ideas presented lack precision and conciseness
The sender of the message does not distance themselves from the facts narrated

question:
A teacher, in the unit of the lyric genre in an 8th Grade class, will conduct a summative evaluation, which contains, among other questions, the following: What is the tone of the following poem?
Despecho
Ah, I am so tired! I have laughed so much,
So much, that tears have appeared in my eyes;
So much, that this grimace that contracts my mouth
Is a strange trace of my wild laughter.
So much, that this intense pallor I have
(Like in old noble portraits)
Is due to the fatigue of the wild laughter
That slides its lethargy over my whole body.
Ah, I am so tired! Let me sleep;
For, like anguish, joy makes you sick.
What a strange occurrence to say that I am sad!
When have you seen me more joyful than now?
Lie! I have no doubts, nor jealousy,
Nor uneasiness, nor anguish, nor sorrows, nor longings,
If my eyes shine with the humidity of tears,
It is due to the effort of laughing so much...
Juana de Ibarbourou
Upon reviewing the evaluations, the teacher finds the following student's response: “The tone of the poem is joy, because the speaker says in several verses that they are laughing.”
What comment from the teacher to the student's answer could favor their identification of the tone of the evaluated poem?
choices: You must explain what the speaker means in the last stanza of the poem, where they establish their stance, and then identify the tone
You managed to grasp that the poem talks about joy. However, the tone still needs to be determined. To do so, I suggest you relate the title to the content of the poem
You identified that the emotion of the poem relates to joy, but you did not recognize the tone. You must identify the lyrical attitude and relate it to the poem's purpose
You remained at a denotative level, failing to recognize the tone of the poem. You must underline the verses where a feeling is explicitly mentioned in the poem to determine which one prevails

question: In a 6th Grade class, in the unit on the lyric genre, a teacher will give the students a written test, which includes a section in which the understanding of the language used in different poems will be evaluated. Which of the following evaluation indicators would address the evaluated learning?
choices: They identify the lyrical motive of the poem
They recognize the lyrical attitude of the speaker of the poem

question: A teacher in a 7th grade class, in the unit on argumentation, will evaluate the following learning objective: "To value the diversity of perspectives, beliefs, and cultures present in their environment", through conducting a debate. Which of the following options presents the evaluation indicator that best responds to the stated learning objective?
choices: They ask others about their position or opinion on a topic
They counter-argue using solid data based on reliable evidence
They ask questions and make comments, out of their own motivation, to delve deeper into a topic
They intervene with respect towards the heterogeneous opinions expressed by their peers

question: A teacher wants to work on the writing of a dramatic play in 1st Grade of secondary school. For this purpose, she asks the students to read a news article and then write a short play in three acts based on the theme of the article. Considering the stages of the writing process, which of the following pedagogical actions best guides the construction of the play's conflict?
choices: Guide the planning process oriented towards the construction of the dramatic conflict
Guide, during the self-correction stage of the play, the identification of the dramatic conflict
Guide the construction of the conflict during the review, modeling self-assessment with a rubric in hand
Guide the construction of the conflict during re-editing, modeling the expected standard concerning the construction of the conflict

question: A high school teacher proposes to work with the students on the identification of pronouns referring to different entities. To achieve this, the teacher provides a table classifying personal, demonstrative, and possessive pronouns, and suggests reading the following short story: Fear of Reality From Monday to Friday, he would take the subway. He would travel all the lines and connections for hours. He knew every station guard. How much longer will he keep lying, they would say to him. Why doesn't he just tell her that he was fired months ago. (Paola Rivera). After the reading, the teacher asks the students about pronouns that refer to entities in the story. A student claims that the word "las" relates to one of the central elements of the story. What difficulty does the student's response reveal in relation to what the teacher requested?
choices: The distinction between the form of pronouns and other grammatical categories
The identification of the entities by relating the word "las" with the word "stations"
The lack of knowledge of the central entities of the story in question: the guards, him, the wife
The conceptual recognition of the different types of pronouns and their specific characteristics

question: A teacher of 2nd grade of secondary school tackles the writing of expository texts. During the activity, he reviews the following statements from texts written by his students: "They have made all efforts to reduce gas emissions, therefore, they have not achieved it" and "No visible changes have been made in the organic waste treatment method, and monetary contributions have arrived to implement them." What is the main difficulty evident in the texts presented by the students?
choices: The impossibility of establishing connectors to advance in writing
The lack of connectors in general in their different semantic relations
The lack of knowledge of semantic relations for textual construction
The incorrect use of connectors to establish relations of opposition between ideas

question: A teacher, who is working on argumentation with a year 3 high school class, reviews the following writing from one of her students: “Expert advisors have stated that, currently, we find ourselves with the highest gas emission index in the last three years.” Which of the following statements would constitute the most appropriate feedback to correct the agreement error presented by the term “highest” in the previous writing?
choices: The passage presents a grammatical disagreement in the term "highest"
The text must be corrected, as it has a number agreement error in the word "highest"
With what element does the adjective "highest" agree in grammatical number?
You should read your text again, find the grammatical error and rewrite it correctly

question: A fourth grade teacher is reading with his students the following excerpt from the story *The Discussion of the Hares,* by Alicia Morel:  Simon the rabbit had a ferocious appetite. He also had a wife, Clarita, and a large family of eight children, because they were "multilittered." On a sunny winter day, one of those where you feel like running and flying across fields and mountains, Simon called his wife to take the family out for fresh air. "Clarita, take advantage of the good weather because it's going to rain tomorrow!" "Are you crazy? Dogs or the fox that lives in the nearby forest could come," she replied, barely poking her nose out of the burrow. "What dogs or foxes! Today is truce day." "Are you sure?" "I'm not brave enough to be up here if today wasn't the day when no hunter can hunt," Simon affirmed, lying back to soak up the sun.  Which of the following questions can the teacher ask for students to make an inference from the text?
choices: What was the weather like the day Simon called his wife?
What did you think of Simon's attitude towards Clarita?
Why did Simon want his wife to take the kids out that day?
What feeling does Clarita convey when she replies to her husband?

question: A teacher of a 4th grade class is designing a test to assess the reading comprehension of her students through various questions related to non-literary texts. Among the selected texts, the teacher includes the following:  Bats are the only mammals equipped with wings capable of flying. One of their characteristics is that they have a very limited sense of sight, so they orient themselves and locate obstacles and food using a developed system of high-frequency ultrasounds inaudible to humans.  They are nocturnal animals that feed on insects and small animals. Like bees and other insects, bats fulfill an important function in nature: they are pollinators without which many plant species could not reproduce.  Although bats are commonly associated with being small animals, there are bats of different sizes. The smallest weighs about 1.5 grams, while the largest can weigh 1.2 kilograms and have a wingspan of 1.5 meters.  Bats are present on all continents, except Antarctica. Like mole rats, they are mammals whose body temperature depends on the environment, especially when inactive.  (Adapted from: www.nationalgeographic.com.es/animales/murcielagos).  Which of the following questions allows evaluating the extraction of implicit information from the previous text?
choices: Why aren't bats found in Antarctica?
Why are bats commonly associated with being small animals?
What characteristic distinguishes bats from other mammals?
Why can't humans hear the sounds bats make?

question: In a higher nursery level, the educational team decides to plan strategies to promote the following learning objective of the Verbal Language core: “To express orally their needs and interests, through the combination of words and gestures, the use of word-phrase and progressively the use of simple sentences.”  Which set of activities is appropriate for the children to address this learning objective?
choices: In the initial circle, ask the children to repeat words from a song. Then, in a new experience, have them follow songs with physical and verbal response. They finish by singing accompanied by percussion instruments

In small groups, ask the children to identify and repeat onomatopoeias of different animals. Then, in a new experience, have them repeat rhymes related to animals. They finish by completing simple sentences with rhymes related to animals

In large groups, invite the children to explore and taste a fruit juice and motivate them to discover its ingredients through riddles. Then, in a new experience, invite them to select by naming the fruits they wish to use to prepare a new juice to taste

Finish by encouraging them to play with the puppet and create stories freely

question: Based on an experimental activity, a third-grade student wrote the following text, in which he explains what happens to the seeds six days after being placed in a moist substrate.  May 12.  With the moist corns, after 6 days, leaves appeared and they can now perform photosynthesis.  Which grammatical aspect needs correcting in the student's writing?
choices: The use of connectors according to their functions
The number agreement between article and noun
The use of verb conjugation according to tenses
The number agreement between the pronoun and the noun it replaces

question: A teacher in a 6th grade class is exercising reading comprehension with the students. As part of the activities, she has them read the following poem with the goal of interpretation:  Butterfly of the air,   how beautiful you are,   butterfly of the air   golden and green.   Light of a lantern,   butterfly of the air   stay there, there, there!   Stay there!   Butterfly, are you there?    (Butterfly, Federico García Lorca).  What reading comprehension strategy would be appropriate to apply after the reading to achieve the proposed objective?
choices: Answer the question: what is the lyrical reason of the poem?
Answer the question: where do you think the butterfly went?
Share with classmates what they know about butterflies
