Pedro has to measure the length of a table, a pencil case, and a classroom. Which objects should he measure in centimeters and which in meters?

question: A teacher of a 2nd Grade class is preparing an assessment for the geometry unit and will include an activity that allows obtaining information about the level of learning their students have achieved in relation to the comparison of 2D shapes. Which of the following activities would allow the teacher to evaluate the aforementioned learning?
choices: Look in magazines for objects that resemble different 2D shapes and cut them out
Mark the vertices of different 2D shapes with a colored point and count them
Classify a group of 2D shapes according to the number of sides they have
Identify the 2D shapes that correspond to the forms of the faces of some 3D figures

question: In a Grade 3 class, a teacher is conducting a lesson with the goal of having students recognize angles in the environment and estimate their measure, using 45◦ and 90◦ angles as a reference. During the development of the class, the teacher drew three intersecting lines on the board to show the difference in measurement between them. Then she asked if they recognized any of those angles in their daily life. A student responded: When I dance in the folklore workshop, the teacher asks us to make a half turn, and he draws it on the board in a similar way. Considering the achievement of the lesson's objective, which of the following teacher's responses best takes advantage of the student's intervention?
choices: Show us on the board the drawing that corresponds to a half turn! What type of angle is formed with a half turn?
Show us the movement that corresponds to a half turn in the cueca! How many degrees is a half turn?
Show us on the board the drawing that corresponds to a half turn! In what other situation have you seen a half turn?
Show us the movement that corresponds to a half turn in the dance! Does a half turn correspond to an angle greater or less than 90◦?

question: An educator places her preschool group in a circle to play a mathematical game. To do this, she uses a box with a slot and cardboard tokens; in the game, she inserts the tokens one by one into the slot of the box, encouraging the group to count aloud. When she finishes inserting the tokens, she asks: How many tokens are in the box? Then, she shakes the box, pours the tokens onto the carpet and asks again: How many tokens are on the carpet? Regarding the learning experience described, what is one of the mathematical skills that the educator is promoting in the boys and girls of her group?
choices: Comparison
Number identification
Numerical sequencing
Conservation of quantity

question: A 12th-grade teacher is planning a class with the objective of "Determining the graphical representation of the inverse function of an invertible function presented graphically". Which of the following skills should students have achieved to meet the proposed objective?
choices: Solve algebraic expressions
Graph functions from tables of values
Perform reflections of figures regarding an axis

question: Which of the following didactic resources is most appropriate to begin working on the representation of two-digit numbers according to their positional value in a 2nd grade class?
choices: Base ten blocks
Coins of $10 and $1
Chips of two different colors
Positional chart with removable digits

question:
A 2nd-grade teacher set the class objective for her students to compare numbers from 0 to 100.
Which of the following performances would allow the teacher to assess if the students achieved the proposed objective?
choices: Match different numbers less than 100 with their pictorial representation
Identify numbers that come before or after a given number less than 100
Decompose three consecutive numbers less than 100 into tens and units
Solve counting problems of numbers less than 100 using the number line

question: A fourth-grade teacher is planning a class in which she will work on comparing decimal numbers. To start, she will ask the students to compare the following numbers: 1.37 with 1.4 and 1.25 with 1.5; for this purpose, she is looking for a type of representation that will help them perform the exercise and understand the content. Which of the following activities would meet the requirement that the teacher has set?
choices: Write the quantities as hundredths
Express the quantities in fractional form
Represent the quantities with concrete materials
Illustrate the quantities in everyday situations

question: A preschool educator is working on the following learning objective: “Communicate the process developed in solving concrete problems, identifying the question, actions, and possible answers.” Considering the above information, which assessment instrument allows the description of the progression of this learning?
choices: Checklist
Holistic rubric
Numerical scale
Rating scale

question:
Amparo, from preschool, plays with spoons of different sizes during zone play. During the game, when arranging them in a row, the girl says: "Oh! It's like a family, this is the dad because it's the largest, this is the mom because it's medium, and this is the son because it's the smallest." The educator has observed her several times engaging in this type of mathematical play.
What mathematical thinking skill underlies Amparo's performance?
choices: Comparison and patterns
Comparison and serial order
Grouping and correspondence
Grouping and sequential order

question: An educator in a preschool setting observes that Ana decides to work with a set of farm animal figures and separates them into three groups that she calls "large farm animals", "medium farm animals" and "small farm animals". On the other hand, Pedro selects building blocks and arranges them by placing small red block, large blue block, small red block, large blue block. Considering the performance of these children, what skill are they developing, respectively?
choices: Ana classifies by one criterion and Pedro creates a pattern with two variable attributes
Ana classifies by two criteria and Pedro creates a pattern with one stable and one variable attribute
Ana establishes correspondence between two groups and Pedro creates a pattern with two stable attributes
Ana establishes correspondence between two groups and Pedro creates a pattern with one stable and one variable attribute

question: A 8th grade teacher is working with their students on the multiplication and division of rational numbers. During the class, a student points out the following: "When I multiply two positive integers, I always get a result greater than those numbers. Does the same happen when I multiply two positive rationals?" Which of the following explanations from the teacher precisely answers the student and, at the same time, facilitates the understanding of the content discussed in the class?
choices: The set of rational numbers is an extension of the set of natural numbers; therefore, the product of positive rationals retains its properties. Let's develop as an example the product of \(\frac{7}{3} \cdot \frac{5}{2}\)

By definition, the result of multiplying positive numbers is always positive; therefore, the product of positive rationals also satisfies this property. Let's develop as an example the product of \(\frac{7}{2} \cdot \frac{5}{3}\)

The product of positive rationals is greater than its factors only if both are greater than 1; therefore, it is enough for one factor to be less than 1 for this to no longer hold. Let's develop as an example the product of \(\frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{5}{2}\)

The pictorial representation of the product of two positive rationals corresponds to the graphical intersection of each of the factors; therefore, the result should be less than these. Let's develop as an example the product of \(\frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{2}{5}\)

question: A teacher of a 7th Grade class is working on the concept of absolute value in integers. During the correction of some exercises presented on the board, a student asks the teacher: "Why is the result negative when there is a negative sign in front of the absolute value? You said that the absolute value of any number is always positive, so I don’t understand why that has to be the case." Which of the following explanations answers the above question accurately, using language understandable for a 7th Grade student?
choices: The negative sign before an expression means "the additive inverse of." Since absolute value is always greater than or equal to zero, its additive inverse will always be less than or equal to zero

The negative sign before an expression also means "change of sign." Since absolute value is always greater than or equal to zero, changing the sign always results in a value that is less than or equal to zero

The negative sign before an expression is equivalent to using the rule of signs in the multiplication of integers. Since absolute value is always greater than or equal to zero, given that "positive times negative is negative," the result will always be less than or equal to zero

The negative sign before an expression is equivalent to having a negative number before a parenthesis. Since the absolute value is always greater than or equal to zero and the negative sign changes the sign inside the parenthesis, its value will always be less than or equal to zero

question: A teacher of an 8th grade class will address the objective "Understand the concept of function relating two variables" through different representations in a sequenced manner. First, he will explain the concept of function using machine metaphors, and then he will show the relationship between the variables of a function through an activity that helps students shift from one register to another. Which of the following activities is consistent with the learning objective and would facilitate this change of register?
choices: Plot a function on the Cartesian plane
Represent a function through a table of values
Identify ordered pairs that belong to a function
Formulate algebraically the expression that represents a function

question:
A teacher will work with their 7th grade students on the learning objective related to understanding the circle as a geometric place, and calculating its perimeter and area.
Which of the following prior knowledge from the areas of Numbers and Algebra can be connected with the geometric concepts that will be worked on in this objective?
choices: Introduction to irrational numbers including the value of π
Inverse proportionality relating the area and diameter of a circle
Operations with decimal numbers for understanding measurement units
Direct proportionality relating the perimeter and diameter of a circle

question: A third grade teacher is working on the characteristics of 3D figures with his students, and has designed an activity to help them get familiar with the concepts of faces, vertices, and edges. Build different 3D figures from their nets
Identify 2D figures and their equivalent in 3D figures

question: A nursery level teacher will carry out a diagnostic evaluation for the infants regarding the following learning objective: "Explore through their sensory and motor experiences, attributes of objects," within the core Mathematical Thinking. During transition moments, show the children different groups of objects that have attributes in common such as color and shape
During variable activity time, encourage the children to discover different objects by listening to the description of their attributes: shape and functionality

question: A 3rd Grade teacher evaluated her students to see if they had learned to identify and describe patterns in 100 charts. Among the tasks given in the evaluation, she presented a chart below and asked what the pattern in the sequence formed by the highlighted numbers was. One student replied that the pattern was to add 1.  (The chart with numbers from 1 to 100)  Which of the following comments from the teacher guides this student towards achieving the objective?
choices: Remember that we are working on patterns and sequences. I propose you color one of the rows in the chart with one color and one of the columns with another color. Look at the numbers in each row and each column. What numbers change in the row? What numbers change in the column? I invite you to create a new chart with the patterns you observed

Remember that we are working on patterns and sequences. In the presented chart, where can you observe a sequence that follows the pattern you indicated in your answer? I propose you circle it with a color. Now, what would happen if we applied the pattern of adding 17 to the sequence in question? I invite you to find these sequences in the chart

And between the second and the third? Will it be the same if you calculate it for all the numbers you circled? What will be the pattern of the sequence you marked? Compare this pattern with the one you previously gave

question: A 6th grade teacher is working with students on a set of exercises about ratios. In previous classes, she worked with them on different ways to represent them. choices: Expressing both ratios as fractions
Representing both ratios using grids
Placing the value of the ratio of both ratios on the number line
Using a real-world situation to exemplify the application of both ratios

question: An 8th grade teacher is working with her students on the Algebra unit, and in her upcoming classes, she will address the objective "To represent inequalities concretely, pictorially, or symbolically." question: In 5th grade, the teacher is developing the following learning objective: "Discover a rule that explains a given sequence and allows for making predictions." Which of the following assessment indicators will verify if the previous objective has been achieved?
choices: They formulate predictions based on a given pattern
They describe the terms of a sequence to find a regularity among them

question: A teacher in 2nd year of high school is planning the classes in which she will address the objective "Order irrational numbers and represent them on the number line".  Which of the following sequences of activities is relevant for students to work on in class and achieve the objective?
choices:

question: One of the learning objectives of the 1st year secondary curriculum is the following: "To develop the rules of probabilities, the additive rule, the multiplicative rule, and the combination of both, in a concrete, pictorial, and symbolic manner, manually and/or with educational software, in the context of problem-solving." Classify the cases in which each formula or rule is used

question: A teacher in a Third-Year class was working with the students on the exponential function and in the next class will work on the logarithmic function. choices: Pose situations modeled by logarithmic functions expressed algebraically, interpreting, together, their domain and range concerning the given context
Project the graphs of different logarithmic functions, each one with its respective inverse exponential function, determining the domain and range of the first, based on the second

question: A teacher in a 2nd year class will work on the following objective: "Analyze the behavior of the graph of a quadratic function of the form f(x) = ax² + bx + c, with a ≠ 0 when its parameters a, b, and c vary," linking it to the curricular emphasis on the use of ICT (Information and Communication Technologies). Create a digital presentation showing different parabolas in their geometric representation and their algebraic relationship

Determine points of a given quadratic function and graph it in geometric software to verify the belonging of these points

question: In a 3rd year class, a secondary teacher is working on the following objective: "Recognize complex numbers as an extension of the numerical field of real numbers." question: The educational team of a preschool class plans to strengthen the appreciation of diversity based on the following learning objective of the core Understanding the Sociocultural Environment: "Recognize significant events in their personal and family history, in various situations." question: Read the following situation: After explaining to the students the importance of memory in people's lives, the teacher sets the learning objective of structuring the elements of memory. question:

question: A teacher introduces the concept of emotion and points out that emotions are intense, but they have a duration proportional to the stimulus that causes them. question: Read the following situation: A teacher explains to her students the difference between primary and secondary socialization. question: Read the following case: A teacher explains Nietzsche's theory on the origin of morality, described in 'On the Genealogy of Morality'. question:
Read the following text:
[...]A group of children is reading a text with information about an indigenous group (diaguitas) that works in ceramics. The text
is accompanied by a picture showing women grinding grains in a mortar, and ceramic pots beside
them.

The tendency to make generalizations in front of situations that present elements of continuity

question: With the intention of characterizing the main economic transformations in Chile after the Great Depression of capitalism, a teacher began the class by asking her students: "How was the 1929 crisis confronted in Chile?" question: Read the following situation: A teacher is developing activities aimed at enabling students to explain the relationships between the Mapuche and Spaniards during the colonial period. They locate the parliament of Paicaví and recount how the border between both groups changed over time

They compare their arguments with those of a classmate about the boundaries of the public and the private in the use of social networks, considering the philosophical references used in class
They construct an argument about privacy norms on social networks, using ideas from classical, modern, or contemporary philosophers

question: A fourth-grade teacher gathers students in groups and asks them to search for information on the Internet about a natural resource of Chile. Then, he asks them to discuss the importance of this resource, what would happen if it disappeared, and how we can protect it today. Finally, each group must present their conclusions to the class. What skill is the teacher primarily aiming to develop through the above activity?
choices: Inquiry
Spatial thinking
Working with sources
Critical thinking

question: A 4th-year high school teacher has explained Kantian critique of the faculties of knowledge and then asks his students to answer some related questions in their notebooks. Upon review, he discovers that a majority of the class confused Kant's answer about the object of knowledge with the empiricists' point of view. What activity would be appropriate for students to understand and differentiate Kant's thought?
choices: Students summarize the main characteristics of empiricist and Kantian thought, noting them in their notebooks
Students conduct research on the thought of Kant and Locke, and then present their main contributions
Students do a comparative analysis of the ideas of empiricists, rationalists, and Kant's ideas, through a conceptual map
Students create a dictionary of Kantian, empiricist, and rationalist terms

question: A 4th year Secondary teacher plans as an objective for their students to analyze and interpret Nietzsche's phrase "there are no facts, only interpretations", for which they have decided to use tools from mass media. Which of the following resources is relevant to address this objective?
choices: Display a fake news story and the evidence that invalidates it
Show edited and real photographs of television characters
Expose two news articles on the same event but with different editorial lines
Present the number of likes and dislikes on a photo about a news story

question: A teacher evaluated the unit on epistemology in the 3rd year of high school, specifically focusing on Cartesian arguments about substance. In the evaluation, he notices that some students express arguments concerning the idea of perfection similar to the following: "According to Descartes, if all people have an idea of what perfection is, it is because we have all once had an experience of something perfect, and thus this idea was imprinted in our minds. And if we all have known something perfect, it is because God created these objects." In relation to Cartesian arguments, what difficulty in the learning process can be inferred from this response?
choices: The students did not manage to synthesize the Cartesian problem regarding the perfect substance originating from our impressions
The students did not understand the Cartesian argument about the idea of perfection as an innate idea originating from reason
The students did not adequately elaborate their statements, confusingly explaining the Cartesian argument about the idea of God that derives from perfection
The students did not adequately organize the argumentative sequence to express the Cartesian argument that infers the existence of God from the idea of perfection

question: An 8th-grade teacher is working on the unit 'The Rise of National Monarchies,' aiming to promote the skill of reading and analyzing sources, specifically the reliability of sources, considering the curricular emphasis on historical thinking formation. To this end, she proposes reading the following source:  No one can deny that the power [...] of the monarchs grew as economic resources and the size of armies increased. Moreover, the law not only protected the subjects but also the legal powers of the princes. Lawyers were one of the main elements of the reform of the monarchies. And this was particularly true in countries where the professionalism of Law [...] had its roots in the laws of ancient Rome [...]  (The Europe of the Reformation. 1517 - 1559, Elton Geoffrey (1999).)  Which of the following activities will directly promote the analysis of the reliability of the source by the students?
choices: Determine the type of source, primary or secondary, based on its year of publication
Establish who Elton Geoffrey is and what his intention was when writing the source
Identify the author's historical perspective on national monarchies
Describe the usefulness of the text about the power of the monarch to understand the rise of national monarchies

question: A teacher in 2nd Grade, in the unit The Bipolar World, will address the following class objective: "Characterize the political-ideological projects of the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War," in coherence with the curricular emphasis of Social Sciences: political and economic perspective.  Considering the context presented, which of the following activities for the students to perform is consistent with the class objective and the proposed curricular emphasis?
choices: Research online about the implementation of the economic models of the United States and the Soviet Union and their effects in the political realm, considering their respective spheres of influence during the Cold War, and then write an essay about it

Create a graphic organizer about the most notable historical events in the political and economic fields of the ideological projects of the United States and the Soviet Union, and then describe in a paragraph the evolution of each during the Cold War

Read secondary sources related to the models of the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War, then write conclusions about their central political elements and the bases of their economic organization, identifying advantages and disadvantages of each model

Create a comparative table to distinguish similarities and differences between the American and Soviet projects during the Cold War, using as criteria of analysis the military and economic alliances established with other countries and their spheres of influence

question: During the unit The Democratic Break, a teacher in a second-level high school class plans to work on the analysis of iconographic sources. Therefore, she has prepared different questions for her students to interrogate the following photograph:  (Photograph of one of the murals of the Ramona Parra Brigade painted in October 1972 and intended to defend the Popular Unity. This photograph was exhibited at the Museum of Contemporary Art. Later rescued in 2002 by Eduardo "Mono" González.)  Which of the following questions is directed at conducting an internal analysis of the photograph as a historical source?
choices: Does the source have bias?
What is the central idea conveyed by the source?
What is the historical context of the source?
Who is the author of the source?

question: A teacher in a 3rd High School class, in the unit Territory, organization, and local participation, after addressing the following objective: "Analyze situations of territorial conflict from the perspective of socio-environmental justice", performs an evaluation activity based on the following case analysis: In our community, during winter, the houses in the Porvenir sector usually experience flooding more than once a year, since there is no stormwater drain, the drains are frequently clogged due to lack of maintenance, and the streets have a low slope. The Porvenir sector has high social vulnerability, as a significant percentage of households are of low socio-economic status. Does the existing territorial conflict in the Porvenir sector relate to socio-environmental justice? Why? When reviewing the evaluation, the teacher encounters the following response: The situation in the Porvenir sector is an example of the lack of good urban planning and the influence of economic inequality on people's lives. However, it is not closely related to socio-environmental justice because it is not an environmental problem. Considering the previous answer, which of the following teacher interventions, as formative feedback, facilitates the student recognizing their error?
choices: I invite you to examine the environmental problems of the area. Is there any impact on the quality of life of the people that can be considered from the perspective of socio-environmental justice?
To deepen your argument, I suggest you evaluate other risks that the population of the Porvenir sector might face. Could these risks become issues of socio-environmental justice?

I suggest you consider the following: is it possible that these factors affect the environmental sustainability of this territory? If so, would it not also affect the access to socio-environmental justice of the people living in that sector?

You should reflect on the following: if the neighborhoods that suffer the most from flooding are the poorest, does it not imply that they are exposed to a risk situation that other social groups do not face? Does this relate to socio-environmental justice?

question: A kindergarten level educator plans to evaluate the achievement of the following learning objective from the Socio-Cultural Environment Understanding core: "Communicate some social stories about significant events from the past of their community and country, using resources such as photographs, videos, utensils, or representative objects."  Which of the following learning experiences allows the gathering of evidence about the achievement of this learning objective?
choices: Invite them to dramatize different festivals from their community
Invite them to give presentations on the role of different characters in their community
Invite them to create an album with different photographs of family celebrations
Invite them to discuss the needs that led to some technological changes

question: A teacher will address with their 7th grade students the unit on The great civilizations of humanity. In the first class, the teacher will teach the students how to select information sources, to work with them on source analysis and to promote the development of historical thinking.  What prior learning do students need to develop in order to appropriately select a historical source?
choices: Identify the types of information that the source provides
Recognize the historical agents to which the source alludes
Evaluate the relevance of the source in relation to the topic to be addressed
Distinguish the central arguments about the process present in the source

question: In a 7th grade class, in the unit on the Middle Ages, a teacher sets as an objective: "Develop historical empathy by distinguishing the frontier relations between Christians, Muslims, and Jews in the Iberian Peninsula." To achieve this, she asks the students to construct a narrative that reflects the relations existing in that time period.  While monitoring the activity, she observes that several students do not recognize the existence of frontier relations between Muslims, Christians, and Jews. For example, she finds several works with content similar to the following: "My name is Muhamed, I am a young Muslim living in the Caliphate of Cordoba, my whole family follows the Muslim religion and we sell carpets in the market. We do not associate with Christians or Jews because they are infidels."  Considering the evidence collected, what new activity can the teacher propose to the students to address the proposed objective, focusing on the development of historical empathy?
choices: Individually describe how they imagine the peoples who lived on the Iberian Peninsula lived and interacted, based on observing images
In groups, represent the different dynamics of coexistence that occurred within the Iberian Peninsula, based on the recording of testimonies from each of the peoples who inhabited it
Complete a chart about the religious beliefs of each of the peoples who inhabited the Iberian Peninsula, based on reading the guidebook, describing how these influenced their relations

Provide examples of the current relations established between Christians and Muslims based on reading news on the internet, pointing out similarities and differences with what happened on the Iberian Peninsula during the Middle Ages

question: Which of the following activities promotes the skill of source analysis by students?
choices: They visit a museum with an exhibition of objects and images from European culture
They select images related to national culture from a set of photographs of various countries
They interview migrants from various countries and present to their classmates the main characteristics of those cultures
They create posters about ways of integrating migrant cultures based on various images and present them to the class

question:
In a first-year high school class, the Technology teacher asks the students to develop a project called "Emprendemás." In this project, the students must create a company that offers a service to address a need of a specific segment of society. When the students present their ideas explaining the need they will address and the service they will offer, the teacher notices that some teams are unable to define the market segment to which the service is directed. 
What activity could the teacher propose so that the students can determine the segment for which the service they want to offer is destined?
choices: Ask the students to analyze the characteristics of the people in whom they detected the need so that they can systematize the information, and then create an empathy map to understand what they want
Ask the teams to watch a video showing the services offered by the competition and determine the type of clients they serve, and then compare them with the potential recipients of their product

Ask the teams to investigate which social segments the competition offers services like those they propose, so that they can analyze them and determine how they differ, defining the value proposition of the service they are offering

Ask the students to create and send an online survey to different people asking if they would use the service they are proposing, and collect data from the respondents, such as age, salary range, profession, nationality, and gender

question: A group of students is planning the design of a technological object that requires a mixed electrical circuit for its operation. Which of the options presents a group of tools necessary for the execution of their project?
choices: Soldering iron, pliers, and saw
Electrical tape, cables, and tweezers
Cables, pliers, and soldering iron
Pliers, soldering iron, and wire stripper

question: Read the following situation: A group of students is tasked with solving the problem of organizing and arranging tools (saws, pliers, measuring tapes, hammers, and miter boxes) in the Technology room. What functional aspects should they consider when designing their object/solution?
choices: That allows storing the tools according to their size, weight, and shape
That allows storing the tools in a way that they are accessible to users
That is made with materials that can withstand the weight and keep the tools isolated from moisture
That is made with waste materials and that are resistant to temperature changes

question: Read the following situation: A teacher wants their 7th grade students to develop interactive stories that they can share with classmates and parents. Which web service is most suitable for carrying out this activity?
choices: Scratch
Excel
WordPress
Vimeo

question: A group of students conducts surveys and interviews for the first time with a certain number of users to understand their needs and desires. What stage of the project does this action correspond to?
choices: Understand the user
Characterize the user
Confirm objectives
Evaluate the project

question:
Read the following situation: 
An interdisciplinary project is designed between Technological Education and Physical Education, whose objective is to promote understanding of the functioning of the skeletal muscle system of the human body.
What content of Technological Education is relevant to apply in this project?
choices: Simple mechanisms as a demonstration of the functioning of muscle groups and their relationship with the skeleton
Electrical circuits as a demonstration of the functioning of the peripheral nervous system
Reuse and recycling in the creation of models of the musculoskeletal system
System concept to illustrate cooperation between the components of the musculoskeletal system

question: In relation to the evolution of the telephone as a technological solution, which of these questions could the teacher ask to generate cognitive conflict in their students?
choices: What advanced functions does a smartphone offer compared to previous phones?
How has the evolution of the telephone been throughout history?
Are smartphones an advance or a setback from a social point of view?
What types of human needs are satisfied with the appearance of smartphones?

question: Read the following situation: Members of an educational community do not read the boards or bulletin boards where relevant information for them is published, for this reason, time and resources are wasted delivering the information repeatedly. In Technological Education, a group of students is challenged to face this problem within their school and propose a technological product to solve it. They begin to develop the different stages of the project methodology; in one of them, they focus on analyzing different written communication media. To which stage of the project methodology does this activity correspond?
choices: Information search, after identifying the need
Solution design in light of research results
Communication of solution designs
Evaluation of the solution and functional tests

question: A group of students complete their weekly work journal. Upon finishing, they submit a Gantt chart to the teacher, in which they establish the tasks assigned to each of the members during the execution of the project. At what stage of their project are the students?
choices: Evaluation
Planning
Idea generation
Execution

question: When students generate a project, they normally jump from the idea to the action, leaving aside the "process" that can guarantee success. This process has several stages, and includes one that is key to the correct definition and evaluation of the solution and to narrowing and facilitating its execution. Which stage does this description correspond to?
choices: To the Gantt chart, which shows the different stages of a correct planning
To brainstorming, which allows showing possible solutions from different perspectives
To problem statement, where what is going to be done is defined
To solution design, which allows representing the solution and verifying if its execution is possible

question: A Science colleague consults the Technology Education teacher about the possibility of carrying out an interdisciplinary activity between both subjects. He wants to work on the subject of circuits, asking the students to design a flashlight that is manually charged. Which of the following options is a relevant response to the interdisciplinary work proposal?
choices: Plan using project-based learning methodology, crossing content and skills from both subjects
Conduct a Webquest for students to learn the technological fundamentals incrementally
Define the content that overlaps in both subjects and design joint classes to address the detected gaps
Plan the classes using some standard associated with ICT to implement student work

question: Which of the following activities is most appropriate if you want to promote the exercise of creative and divergent thinking in students?
choices: Pose a real-world problem and ask students for possible solutions to solve it
Provide common-use objects and ask for ideas on how to use them in a completely different way
Request an online investigation on the different ways to manufacture a technological object
Show a video about the Industrial Revolution and ask for a written report on how technology changed society

question: A group of students expresses to their Technology Education teacher their interest in programming but indicate that they do not know how to approach the subject as they consider it very complicated. What pedagogical action by the teacher could stimulate the students and facilitate their access to the subject?
choices: Introduce students to source codes of programs they know and use in their daily lives
Introduce students to programming languages that are familiar to them, such as Java, C++, or PHP
Introduce students to examples of simulators that support the understanding of linear data uses
Introduce students to the basic elements used in programming, such as algorithms, applied to real-life situations

question: Consider the following situation: In Technological Education, students work with project methodology to set up the “Sustainable Fair”, open to the community, where each group must set up a booth to present the products or exhibition they have designed and produced, all within the framework of sustainable development. The work process has been evaluated through observations and the submission of two written reports. The teacher designs the final project evaluation, scheduled once the fair with the stands of each group has been set up. What is the most appropriate evaluative procedure for the final project evaluation, considering the nature of the learning involved in this experience?
choices: A written test of open-ended questions that evaluates the understanding of the concept of sustainable development involved in the work of the various groups in this project
A final written report by group, gathering information from the different steps implemented in the project
A rubric that evaluates the different dimensions of each group's work at the fair, applied both by the teacher and the students themselves
An individual work form in which each student presents their experience about the group work developed during the project

question: A professional technical teacher needs to assess the performance of their students in carrying out a complex practical task at the end of the unit. The execution of this task involves various dimensions and areas to be assessed. Which of the following instruments is most appropriate for evaluating the performance of the students?
choices: Rubric
Checklist
Rating scale
Evidence portfolio

question: In vocational technical education, which of the following methodological strategies allows procedural learning objectives to be addressed more directly?
choices: Role plays
Field trip
Guided demonstration
Problem solving

question:
In the Technology class, 5th-grade students are building a scale model of a car designed by them, using various materials and tools, including some for cutting.
What is the first instruction the teacher should give to the students for them to use the cutting tools safely?
choices: Organize the workplace before carrying out the cutting task
Select a solid and regular surface to make cuts on
Check that the tools are in good condition and have the appropriate edge
Choose the cutting tool based on the task and the material they will work with

question: A group of students identified the need to improve the irrigation system for green areas at their school. Therefore, they decided to implement a new drip irrigation system in these areas. Considering environmental care, which of the following aspects should the teacher take into account to evaluate the implemented solution?
choices: The variation in water consumption once the drip irrigation system is implemented
The extent of green areas that could be covered with the drip irrigation system
The community's assessment of the drip irrigation system in terms of its contribution to the protection of green areas
The use of biodegradable materials (pipes, taps, connections, and others) for the implementation of the drip irrigation system

question: During Technology class, the topic of household organic waste utilization is discussed. The students share experiences related to this issue and recognize the environmental impact this practice can have. Given the large amount of information available online regarding this topic, the teacher proposes creating reading material about organic waste recycling. The teacher decides to use ICT to create this material, what type of document is most suitable for encouraging individual student research?
choices: An online questionnaire
A hypertext document
An online study guide
A presentation in Prezi

question: During the development of a service project, the high school work groups present a series of difficulties to their guiding teacher. In response to one of them, the teacher recommends the preparation of a Gantt chart. Considering the above recommendation, what could have been the difficulty faced by this group?
choices: The supplies needed to develop our service do not match the available resources
We have many information sources available on the Web and do not know which one will be useful for each task
There are many tasks we must perform and we fear losing focus, wasting the limited time we have to reach the goal
The problem we detected has many feasible alternative solutions, we need a criterion to choose which one is the most appropriate

question: A teacher asks the students of Year 9 to make a presentation about the evolution of a technological object of their interest. What can the teacher recommend to the students as the most pertinent sources of information for their research?
choices: Printed sources, especially books and magazines that refer to the selected object
Texts that contain updated and novel information about the selected object
Digital sources that contain relevant information regarding the object they have selected
Magazine articles or texts that are backed by recognized organizations and that are related to the selected object

question: In the context of the First Year High School Technology Learning Objective: “Infer, from the evolution of technological products and environments, the positive and/or negative effects that these have had on society,” the teacher describes the following situation: About 40 years ago, it was customary for families to use cloth diapers to change their babies. Over time, this item was replaced by disposable diapers. Currently, the latter continue to be used massively; however, alternatives have appeared that seek the reuse of diapers. Then, the teacher asks the students to investigate these new alternatives using different sources of information and to prepare a presentation on the evolution of diapers, explaining their social and environmental impact over time. Which of the following indicators would allow the evaluation of whether the presentations are consistent with the stated learning objective?
choices: Describe the changes in diaper design over the last 40 years
Specify some consequences of the emergence of disposable diapers in the daily lives of families
Present how diaper production processes have changed based on their evolution
Communicate testimonies of users who have taken actions to mitigate the harmful effects of diaper use on the environment

question: In a Middle School Technology class, the stage of service design is being worked on. The teacher has asked the work groups to make a presentation that reflects the progress in this stage of the projects. From the project methodology, what is the relevance of presenting progress to the class in the design stage?
choices: To work collaboratively, demonstrating the commitment of the team and openness to receive feedback and opinions from classmates regarding their service
To analyze the impact that the service implementation has generated so far and to formulate improvements that allow the achievement of the project's objective
To contribute productively to the discussion to justify the decisions made in the execution of the service based on the service's objective
To communicate the advances in the service definition, to receive the contribution of each group's opinions and incorporate improvements based on the initial objective

question: Which of the following activities is the most appropriate to evaluate the development of attitudes in the area of safety and risk prevention under a competency-based approach?
choices: Execution of a practical simulation exercise
Preparation of a written report on current regulations
Application of a written test with development questions
Conducting an oral examination on a case study

question: The management team of a professional technical high school, along with the teachers, is working on the following processes: Analysis of requirements coming from the Institutional Educational Project. Analysis of requirements from the local productive environment. Analysis of employment dynamics and the socio-cultural characteristics of the students and the educational community. At what stage of curriculum management is this high school working?
choices: Relevance of evaluation criteria
Units diagnosis
Resource feasibility
Programs contextualization

question:
For the development of projects to create technological objects, a teacher of a 8th grade class challenges his students to use scrap materials as a requirement for the constructive projects they propose.
Which of the following criteria would underlie the requirement that the teacher is asking his students?
choices: Ethical
Technical
Efficiency
Functionality

question:
The technology and science teachers of a 5th grade have agreed to work in parallel on the following science topic: the growth of a plant. For this, the technology teacher has asked her students to develop an explanatory presentation of this process, in order to reinforce the knowledge acquired in science and, additionally, to create an educational material for the 3rd grade students, who also need to learn this process.
Which of the following digital tools is the most appropriate for developing the presentation, considering the purpose and the level of the students?
choices: PowerPoint, using text and images
Movie Maker, recording and editing a video
AnimatorDV, to make an animation of the process
Padlet, publishing useful content to understand the process

question: The students in a 5th Grade class have been working on the unit addressing the Learning Objective "Design technological objects to solve problems, analyzing and modifying products." They have had to identify unresolved problems in their homes and choose an object that, with some modification, could solve them. They must present the results of their work to the class to receive feedback from their peers. Which of the following pairs of indicators would be appropriate to include in the evaluation guideline used by the students to provide feedback to their peers in achieving the objective?
choices: They select a product that can respond to the identified need in the home. They propose changes to the product using drawings or diagrams
They identify a possible solution for an identified need in the home. They name and explain the actions necessary for the improvement of the technological object
They name and describe the steps necessary for the improvement of the technological object. They select and explain the technique to be used for the improvement of the object
They identify the environmental and social effects of the resources used. They select the materials and tools necessary for each part of the object to be modified

question: In the context of the unit “Creating Innovative Designs of Objects or Technological Systems”, a group of 6th-grade students has generated a project proposal in which they will use disposable plastic bottles tied with raffia to build a bench in the yard of their school. The justification they provide is that it would be an innovative object because it would be made from an unusual material that would withstand rain and sun. Which of the following comments would allow the teacher to give feedback to the students from the perspective of functionality?
choices: “Very good work. You managed to address a relevant and familiar problem for your context. However, you still need to specify the characteristics of the material you will use, such as rigidity and hardness.”

“Very well. You have managed to design an innovative object using recycled material, but you need to consider how you will position and connect the bottles so that it can support the weight of the people who use it.”

“Congratulations. Your project is relevant and feasible to carry out, as it considers a proposal that will help the environment by reducing waste generation, but I suggest checking the accessibility to the space you will use.”

“Good team project. I invite you to compare your project with others of similar characteristics, such as park and shopping mall benches, observing the features that make them more comfortable for people.”

question: In the context of the unit "Evaluation and functioning of the solution", the teacher of an 8th grade class plans one of his lessons, with the purpose of redesigning the selected technological product, based on the information gathered in user tests. Which of the following skills should the teacher reinforce beforehand to address the stated objective?
choices: Apply graphic expression and representation methods
Identify basic elements and resources of graphic design
Know data analysis techniques and draw conclusions
Know information collection instruments and their characteristics

question: A teacher in an 8th grade class is working on the following objective: "Reflect and evaluate the feasibility and social and environmental impact of a technological project." During the class, the teacher explains to the students the social impact of some technological solutions, but some students report not understanding the relationship between technological developments and the social field. In response, the teacher decides to use an example. Which of the following examples would allow the teacher to illustrate his explanation?
choices: The invention of the telephone, which allowed a different way of communication and enabled the development of new technology in telecommunications
The creation of the Internet, which allowed the generation of new economic pathways that enable different forms of financial and business management
The invention of machines and steam engines, which allowed an increase in industrial production in less time, making it possible to reach a broader market
The invention of vaccines, which has allowed the control of disease outbreaks, improving people's life expectancy and establishing public policies in this area

question: In a conversation with students from an 8th grade class, regarding the impact of technological solutions, a teacher introduces the concept of planned obsolescence (PO), commenting on the effects it has on the accumulation of technological waste. When discussing how to tackle this phenomenon, the students express skepticism and share various opinions about how difficult it is to reverse the general market trend of producing and selling in large quantities. Which of the following explanations from the teacher would clearly address the students' concerns and promote the skills expected to be developed in the subject?
choices: “Indeed, the phenomenon of PO shows us that the development of technology has disadvantages at various levels and cannot be idealized without any questioning, or we will be causing irreversible environmental damage.”

“Since this is a global problem, it is clear that the commitment of all countries is required for its solution; therefore, we must be attentive to the different summits and conferences that will allow agreements also at a global level.”

“The market does not operate on its own, it responds to consumer demand, and this problem indicates that we must analyze and review our consumption habits to see how we are contributing to this vicious circle and how we could reverse it.”

“Hence the importance of societies being active promoters of change, as social movements are doing by publicly denouncing this problem so that authorities react, for example the SOP (Without Planned Obsolescence) movement.”

question: A Technology teacher for 2nd year high school, about to start a project work, decides to apply a diagnostic evaluation to their students to verify the knowledge and understanding of the stages of a project, which had already been covered the previous year. Considering the purpose and content to be evaluated, which of the following evaluation instruments is most appropriate?
choices: A list of statements that collects the predominant ideas in the course about the different activities that are carried out in each stage of a project
A checklist that contains the quality indicators that must be present in the development of each stage of the project and that allows them to be verified in practical work
A written test with constructed response questions, in which, given a case, identify the different stages of a project and justify their answers
A performance rubric with the classification criteria of the level of mastery demonstrated over the stages of the project, as they develop each one of them in group work

question: The high school students are in the planning stage of their project. To help them develop their plans, the teacher decides to dedicate a class to learning how to work with PERT diagrams, in which they must establish the dependency relationships of the activities for implementing their project. At the end of the class, the teacher decides to formatively assess the students' understanding of what these diagrams are and their usefulness, in order to adjust the planning of the next class based on the given responses. Which of the following instruments allows the teacher to quickly and concretely gather information about the students' understanding and the usefulness of PERT diagrams?
choices: A peer evaluation form, in which students ask each other, “How to construct a PERT diagram,” and then co-correct their answers
An exit ticket, asking students to indicate three things they have learned from the class and two questions they still have about what PERT diagrams are and what they are useful for
A conceptual estimation scale, with categorization of the students' degree of understanding based on their responses to the question: “What is a PERT diagram?”

A questionnaire where students must answer what they have learned about what a PERT diagram is and what it is used for, according to the following categories: “I know it well; I know, but I cannot explain it; and I do not know”

question:
A 10th grade teacher requests their students to conduct research about efficiency in the use of energy resources. One of the groups presents a project in which they conclude that the devices that use less electricity are the most efficient, which does not match the classification of these devices in the energy efficiency table.
What would be the difficulty underlying the students' performance in the presented situation?
choices: They relate the concept of energy efficiency to the use of devices that utilize non-conventional energy sources
They associate the concept of energy efficiency with the lower energy usage in devices that receive the same work
They understand the concept of energy efficiency as energy saving, without considering that the work or service performed by the devices is the same
They identify the concept of energy efficiency as the prevention of unnecessary energy use in performing the work or service of the analyzed devices

question: A teacher of 8th grade, given the importance of addressing topics related to climate change in the Technology class, proposes an activity for her students to work on the theme "Production processes in Chile and clean production." Which of the following activities promotes the critical analysis of this theme more, in accordance with the curricular emphasis of the subject?
choices: The students, divided into groups, visit local companies to learn more about the processes involved in production. Then, they prepare a report with the information obtained from the visits and their opinion about the production processes observed

The students, organized in groups, investigate and create a list of production processes in different economic sectors of the country (agricultural, mining extraction, manufacturing industry, among others), from which they derive causes that explain climate change

The students watch a video describing how Chilean legislation has been updated so that production systems, whether goods or services, move towards clean production processes, achieving the goal of carbon neutrality by the year 2050

The students seek information about some production processes of Chilean companies and compare them with similar companies that have signed clean production agreements. Then, they develop a proposal for the former on how to increase efficiency and reduce environmental risks

question:
In a 7th-grade class, at the end of the first lesson of the unit Creating objects to solve problems, a teacher assigns a task to groups of students to investigate a problem in their home kitchens, which they can later solve by constructing a technological object. In the next class, they are asked to make a drawing of the technological object, with three views and dimensions to scale. One of the groups draws a cereal dispenser, and the teacher observes that the base has a very small opening in proportion to the size of the container, which would impede the flow of cereal.
Which skill pertaining to the subject needs to be reinforced in this group of students, based on the problem detected in their work?
choices: The application of scales, to achieve the graphical representation of the object the students wish to construct
The execution of the design, through which the students address the functionality of the object they wish to construct
The planning, from which the students establish the matrices for the construction of the object they wish to construct
Problem-solving, through which the students must find a solution to the problem detected in their home kitchens

question:
In the framework of achieving better utilization of energy resources, a teacher of a 6th-grade class guides her students in creating different objects. One of the groups built a "magic pot", aiming to optimize the use of gas when cooking food. The teacher decides to create a specific evaluation indicator for the following objective: "Test and evaluate the effectiveness of their technological product".
Which of the following indicators would show that the students are achieving the stated objective?
choices: They specify the functions and usage characteristics that the "magic pot" must meet in relation to energy savings
They analyze known systems (such as the "magic pot") that use unconventional energy and achieve efficient energy management
They experimentally determine the differences in energy expenditure between the "magic pot" and other similar cooking methods
They create a simple "magic pot" and relate its operation to the use of unconventional energy and efficient energy management

question: A teacher of a 7th Grade will evaluate her students with the following unit objective: “Propose adaptation or improvement solutions that have an impact in the environmental context.” In this scenario, the teacher presents the problem of the excess waste generated by humans today, specifically referring to plastic straws. Addressing the issue presented by the teacher, which of the following evaluative activities allows demonstrating the achievement of the expected learning for the unit?
choices: Ask the students to design an individual liquid container and ensure its content can be consumed without the need for a straw
Ask the students to design a communication campaign that promotes the use of reusable bottles, highlighting the positive aspects of this measure
Ask the students to conduct research on non-polluting materials and choose one that can be used in a liquid container
Show the students different existing juice containers and ask them to infer two environmental impacts of each based on functional and economic criteria

question:
A teacher presents to her 8th-grade students, as the class topic, the consequences of excessive screen use on school performance. After introducing the topic, she asks the students to search for information on it on the Internet.
What suggestion can she give to the students so they can obtain precise information about the topic posed on different digital search engines?
choices: Search for preliminary sources and other databases, opting for those belonging to recognized or representative organizations, trying first to find the main websites by their domain name: .org (organization), .gov (government and official agencies) and .edu (education). Use a phrase that correctly delimits what is being searched for, or specify words in the search engine, in order to restrict the results

Start with a broad search of results, using conjugated words, for example: using screens, without quotes. Then narrow down the search by writing more detailed phrases, for example: using screen for more than 8 straight hours. And configuring the country, language, keywords, and the topic's update period. Place the phrase in quotes and use the signs + and –, to add a keyword or remove those we don't want

Choose an efficient and fast search engine (remember that the more databases a search engine accesses, the slower it is). Then search for the information by selecting the country about which you want to find out and the category of the topic, for example: science, technology, entertainment, sports. For the search, use generic words, do not use accents or capitals; if you know how an expression should appear, type it as such enclosed in quotes, with all the words

First create a work plan that contains, in one of the stages of the process, the collection and gathering of references on the topic being investigated. Upon reaching this stage, go to the sources of information, such as books, magazines, documents, databases on the Internet, where the topic is seriously analyzed. Pay close attention to capitals and lowercase letters when writing the articles. Be concerned with accents in the word or phrase to be searched for, to specify the search and narrow the results

question: A 8th grade teacher, in a class to introduce the topic, shows the video “Chile, the best adventure tourism destination in the world”. Then, the teacher asks the students to investigate in groups on the internet about the tourist places in the country, using criteria for the reliability of the information and its sources. In the investigation, what action should the students take to meet these criteria?
choices: Check the authorship and updating of the information
Check the accessibility of the information and the possibility of editing the data
Check the content of the website and if it has a high number of visits
Check the functionality of the website and that the content is a static resource

question: A high school teacher addresses the students with the following learning objective: "Identify possible positive or negative impacts of current technological innovations on the environment and society." After giving the presentation and explaining how technological advances are limited by the low availability of some resources necessary for their development, the teacher realizes that the relationship is still not clear enough and decides to incorporate an example to complement his explanation. Which of the following examples would be appropriate for the teacher to use to illustrate his explanation?
choices: The limitations in the expansion purposes of a factory because it does not have the necessary economic resources to do so
The lack of planning and commitment from local municipalities prevents investment and improvement in the development of rainwater collector technology
The construction of a public works project, such as a road, that faces restrictions because the land needed is owned by the private sector
The decision by some automobile companies to stop producing internal combustion vehicles due to the future scarcity of fossil fuels

question: In a first-year high school class, a teacher introduces the unit on the Evolution of Technological Objects, explaining the concept of innovation through images of various objects created centuries ago, which still remain relevant today. After the explanation, a student asks: "I have a question, an invention, which is something totally new, isn't that the same as an innovation?" What explanation could the teacher give the student to clarify this doubt?
choices: An invention is an innovation when it is truly original and unprecedented. The same applies to modifications made to an object; if they stand out for their great originality, then they are innovations

An invention is always an innovation because new knowledge and technologies are applied to construct it. The same happens with an object that has been modified, as it involves the use of new technologies

An invention is the application of a discovery of a phenomenon that was hidden or unknown, whereas innovation corresponds to the materialization of new technological ideas in modifying existing objects or systems

An invention involves making an idea tangible by converting it into something concrete that did not exist before, and when this is useful to a group of people, fully meeting a need, it then becomes an innovation

question: In Grade 11's unit on Contributions to the Community, a teacher asks students to apply the concept of sustainability in their service projects. During the class, a group of students tells the teacher: "It is impossible to develop a truly sustainable service because what would be needed is to try to minimize the use of natural resources as much as possible, so in that case, a better option is not to produce a service." What explanation is most appropriate to clarify, with conceptual precision and comprehensive language, the students' statement?
choices: Sustainability conditions are those that ensure the existence of the human race for as long as possible, and these conditions can be achieved through zero population growth and a steady state economy or zero economic growth

Sustainable development conditions refer to the concern of making the use of natural resources increasingly efficient and prudent, so that they are not depleted and are preserved for future generations, without simultaneously affecting everyone's access to the products derived from them

Sustainability is the state or quality of life in which human aspirations are satisfied while maintaining ecological integrity. This implies that our current actions must allow interaction with the environment and that human aspirations are sustained over time

Sustainability is defined concerning the carrying capacity of geo-systems to support humanity's development, which implies that the economic system must remain within the carrying capacity limits of the world, understanding sustainability as development without growth

question:
In the unit Efficient Use of Resources, from the 2nd year of high school, a group of students proposes the creation of a manual with different solutions to help selected families from the educational community reduce the cost and consumption of resources such as water, gas, and electricity, and then check if these proposed solutions were useful.
Which set of actions carried out by the group of students indicates that they are capable of evaluating the economic impact of their solution?
choices: The students send an online survey to each family one month after delivering the manual of solutions, asking which of the proposals were implemented in their homes, what difficulties they encountered, and which could be adopted as habits

The students ask the families for their consumption bills, and then they deliver the manual. After a month, they request another bill to compare the results. With this data, they analyze the impact of their solutions

One month after distributing the manual, the students conduct interviews with the families, asking about each member's experience with the application of the proposed solutions. From there, they draw conclusions about the economic impact generated by the solution

Before delivering the manual, the students ask the families: What practices might be causing higher resource consumption in your homes? One month after delivering the manual, they ask again: Which of the proposed solutions helped reduce the expenses?

question: A teacher of 1st year high school is working on the unit "Evolution and impact of a solution". At the end of the unit, the teacher will evaluate the following objective: "Analyze the ways in which technological products and social environments evolve by characterizing the various factors that influence this change." Which of the following activities allows the teacher to evaluate the level of achievement of the stated objective?
choices: Ask the students to explain how a technological development affects society and the environment at a specific time and place
Ask the students to mention the characteristics that society has had in the last 50 years and point out the changes that have required technological solutions
Ask the students to select and describe a concrete example where a technological solution that has evolved over time is related to the changes that society has experienced

Ask the students to, based on interviews conducted with relevant actors in the production areas they studied, identify products, processes, or techniques that have evolved, and point out the aspects that have influenced this evolution

question:
In a 10th grade classroom, a teacher is working with students on the following objective: “Understand the origin and impact of sources of atmospheric pollution.” As an activity, the teacher asks the students to work in groups to research these sources and their impacts, and to prepare a PowerPoint presentation with the information they found. As the groups present their work, the teacher notices that most students conclude that sources of atmospheric pollution are only anthropogenic.
Which of the following comments by the teacher would correspond to formative feedback aimed at guiding students to improve their work and achieve the objective?
choices: Very good, you have shown that human activities have a great negative impact on the atmosphere. However, what other types of atmospheric pollution sources exist that are not related to human activity? What are the impacts of these pollution sources?

Excellent, in your presentation you emphasized that we are all affected by air pollution. The only thing left to do would be to complement this research by answering what technological solutions are sources of atmospheric pollution? What can you propose to lessen the impact of these sources?

Very good work, you have identified that fossil fuels are sources of air pollution due to their massive use in a variety of human activities. However, what do you think is the environmental and social impact of using these fossil fuels? How could these impacts be reduced?

Congratulations, you correctly pointed out the impact of carbon monoxide as a major air pollutant. But you should also ask what is the share of carbon monoxide emissions from private cars in atmospheric pollution? How much could we contribute to mitigation by using public transportation?

question: A teacher in 1st year of secondary education asks his students to prepare a Gantt chart to plan the service they intend to carry out at the institution. During its preparation, the teacher notices that the students are not correctly calculating the time it will take them to carry out each of the activities and, therefore, they will not be able to complete the preparations for the execution of the service on time. Which of the following interventions by the teacher will allow the students to reorient their work to accomplish the requested task?
choices: Show the students an example of a daily activity in which it is required to consider the necessary time to carry out the next one
Ask the students to visualize their project objective and from it derive all the steps to follow to carry out the proposed activity
Present the students with a hypothetical situation where it is observed that the protagonists cannot carry out an activity because they have not done another that is required beforehand
Together with the students, carry out an analysis of the nature of the established activities, relate them to the assigned times, and evaluate whether the latter are appropriate

question: In the unit Development and implementation of a service in a 1st grade secondary class, a teacher is starting to work with their students on the formulation of group projects for the semester. For this, the first objective they will address is: "Identify needs and opportunities that involve the creation of a service". What sequence of activities should the teacher work with their students to address the objective?
choices: The teacher introduces the concept of need and service and provides some concrete examples of both concepts. Afterwards, they ask the students to describe and classify a set of different services in groups according to the type of need they satisfy

The teacher presents cases of needs that have arisen from different historical contexts and that have been resolved through a specific service. Afterwards, they ask them to investigate what contexts have triggered two new services typical of the 21st century

The teacher asks the students what they understand by need. They write down the common definition they arrive at. Then, they give examples and ask the students to discuss in groups which of these can be resolved by a technological product. Once they have completed the plenary, they provide some techniques for identifying needs

The teacher defines the concept of need and gives some examples to the students. Afterwards, they ask them to carry out an investigative work on services present in their environment. They request them for the next class to prepare a work in which they mention the services and describe the solution they offer

question: A group of 1st year students creates a lost items return service in their course. The peculiarity of their service is that when returning an item, they take special care to contact the person and deliver it anonymously to protect those affected from comments or unfounded accusations.  Which of the following indicators allows evaluating whether the students effectively developed their service project considering ethical criteria?
choices: They reflect on the importance of respecting the privacy and safety of people in the development of solutions
They review their solution to assess whether it meets the users' requirements and the care and safety of the same
They define control mechanisms to ensure that the service is carried out respecting the care and privacy of individuals
They implement the service according to the established plan ensuring the protection and safety of the users who utilize it

question: A secondary teacher in 2nd Grade, in the unit "Anthropic Environmental Impacts", has asked their students to collaboratively research the causes of atmospheric pollution associated with industrialization and mass consumption, and the consequences this has in the short and long term. At the end of the work, the teacher asks the students to synthesize the results of their research by establishing the causes and effects of pollution, and to propose short- and medium-term actions to mitigate these impacts.  What evaluation tool allows the teacher to assess the work process performed by the team of students?
choices: Portfolio
Checklist
Rating scale
Student log

question: Which of the following artistic expression activities offers greater opportunities for the development of creativity in children?
choices: Painting with watercolor a mandala model
Folding figures using different types of paper
Modeling with clay the tree that is seen from the living room
Pasting colored papers inside different shapes

question: According to Bowlby's theory, which of the following statements corresponds to a characteristic of attachment?
choices: It is a process that lasts until the early years of life
It is a bond that must be stable and continuous to ensure proper development
It is a bond that determines all affective relationships in life and development
It is the first relationship of the newborn with its mother and cannot be replaced by another person

question: Read the following situation: An educator is starting to work on identifying numbers to develop quantification skills in preschoolers. As a first activity, she wants the boys and girls to be able to identify the number 1. Given her knowledge of the level, she knows that Vicente is an active child, who learns much better by using his body, so she will ask him to imitate a number 1. On the other hand, she also knows that Martina and Clemente have many musical skills and learn quickly through songs, so she will include some in the experience. Which pedagogical principle of Early Childhood Education is mainly highlighted in the planning of this educator?
choices: Empowerment
Uniqueness
Relationship
Play
